# AGENTS.md — read this first

## What we're building

**ReqFlow** is a hackathon prototype for the BMW challenge _"AI for Product Decision Making"_: a
**native desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux** (Electron, not a web app) with three tabs. On
**Data Flow**, an n8n-style flow of **building blocks** (Custom, Raw, Research, AI Filter, AI Splitter,
HIL, Add to Car; some expand into their own inner workplace) turns customer and market data into
prioritized, evidence-linked car requirements. The **Car** tab shows them for the PM to review, and
**Settings** configures the app, global parameters and collaboration. Full spec: [PRODUCT.md](PRODUCT.md). Your task: [docs/WORKSTREAMS.md](docs/WORKSTREAMS.md).
Current state and handoffs: [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md).

## The challenge in brief (from `context/`)

- **Goal:** help BMW product managers define, justify and prioritize **customer-facing requirements
  for the successor** of an existing vehicle, thinking **3–5 years ahead**. The PM stays in control of
  every decision.
- **Vehicles and markets:** the 1, 5 or 7 Series, in Europe, China or the US. Demo **one derivative in one
  market** (ours: 1 Series F70, EU), but don't build a one-off.
- **BMW provides, per vehicle:** customer feedback, equipment data, sales volumes and a customer study.
  We may add web sources such as competitors, reviews and market or technology trends.
- **The app must:** ingest the data and enrich it from the web → extract signals (complaints, unmet needs,
  competitor advantages, trends), **each linked to its sources** → derive clear, actionable, realistic
  requirements → prioritize them with explainable logic → let the PM approve, reject, edit or challenge
  them → record everything in an **audit trail** (who or what, when, and why).
- **Each requirement needs:** a unique ID, an actionable description, linked findings and sources, a
  priority or score, the prioritization rationale, an evidence level, assumptions and uncertainties, and
  a decision status.
- **In scope:** features, equipment, comfort, space, usability, infotainment and digital services,
  design and quality perception, driving experience, range and charging as the customer experiences them,
  and variants and packages. **Out of scope:** regulatory and homologation topics, engineering specs, and
  pricing or business cases (rough effort may be used as a priority factor).
- **Judges value:** trustworthy sources, transparent reasoning, thoughtful prioritization, honest
  handling of uncertainty and **conflicting evidence**, and focus on customer value. Depth in one area
  beats shallow coverage of everything.
- **BMW process we mirror:** situation analysis → structure and context (classify, cluster, dedupe) →
  requirements definition (measurable targets and acceptance criteria) → prioritization (customer and

## Rules for every agent

1. **Stay in your lane.** Edit only the paths your workstream owns (see WORKSTREAMS.md). Do you need
   something changed elsewhere? Write it in your final report instead of editing it yourself.
2. **`packages/core` is the contract.** Build against it and don't change it on your own. If you need a
   contract change, propose it in your final report. The lead merges contract changes.
3. **No real data in git, logs or transcripts.** BMW files go in `data/raw/` (gitignored). Entire
   publishes session transcripts, so when you inspect them, print only structure and counts (sheet
   and column names, row counts), never cell values, and never send them to delegated agents.
   Committed tests use synthetic data (`@reqflow/core/fixtures`, `data/samples/`). Never commit or
   print API keys.
4. **No silent failures.** Validate inputs with the Zod schemas, throw clear errors, and never invent
   sources or evidence. Every finding needs a verbatim excerpt.
5. **AI never decides.** Only a human sets `approved`, `rejected` or `deferred`. Every change to a
   requirement writes an AuditEvent.
6. **Prove it works.** Add colocated `*.test.ts` files. Before you report done, run
   `npm run typecheck && npm test` from the repo root. For UI work, also run `npm run smoke` and look at
   the screenshots in `apps/desktop/out/smoke/`.
7. **Respect the process split.** UI code (renderer) has no Node, no `fs` and no network. It talks to the
   main process only through `api` from `@/lib/api` (contract: `packages/core/src/ipc.ts`). Data, AI
   calls, files and API keys live in the main process. Build paths with `node:path` so they work on Windows.
8. **Sessions are tracked with [Entire](https://github.com/entireio/cli).** Commit with plain `git`.
   Entire attaches your session to each commit as a checkpoint and pushes it on `git push`. Don't
   remove its hooks (`.claude/settings.json`, `.git/hooks`) and never put secrets in prompts.

9. **Hand off in [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md).** Claim your workstream there when you start; your
   tasks are the checklist in its section, in priority order. Update your own section (and only that
   one) when you finish a slice, get blocked or stop: tick done tasks, add a log entry. The next agent
   starts from it. The repo and Entire transcripts are **public**, so never paste keys or BMW data anywhere.

8:   item: PrimaryItem;
9:   context: PipelineData;

11: export type Membership = Record<DataKey, Set<string>>;
12: export function emptyMembership(): Membership {
13:   return Object.fromEntries(DATA_KEYS.map((key) => [key, new Set<string>()])) as Membership;
14: }

16: /** Validate without using the parsed copy: Zod strips upstream extension/provenance fields. */
17: export function validateInput(input: PipelineData): void {
18:   PipelineData.parse(input);
19:   for (const key of DATA_KEYS) {
20:     const ids = new Set<string>();
21:     for (const item of input[key]) {
22:       if (ids.has(item.id)) throw new Error(`AI Splitter input has duplicate ${key} ID ${item.id}`);
23:       ids.add(item.id);
24:     }
25:   }
26:   const records = new Map(input.records.map((r) => [r.id, r]));
27:   for (const finding of input.findings) {
28:     for (const evidence of finding.evidence) {
29:       const record = evidence.recordId ? records.get(evidence.recordId) : undefined;
30:       if (!record) continue; // Partial envelopes are allowed, but unavailable references are logged below.
31:       if (record.sourceId !== evidence.sourceId) {
32:         throw new Error(`Finding ${finding.id} evidence source does not match record ${record.id}`);
33:       }
34:       if (!record.text.includes(evidence.excerpt)) {
35:         throw new Error(`Finding ${finding.id} excerpt is not verbatim in record ${record.id}`);
36:       }
37:     }
38:   }
39: }

41: export function primaryLayer(input: PipelineData): PrimaryLayer | undefined {
42:   return (["requirements", "themes", "findings", "records"] as const).find(
43:     (key) => input[key].length,
44:   );
45: }
46: 
47: /** Stable original objects and envelope metadata, never schema-parsed copies. */
48: export function select(input: PipelineData, membership: Membership): PipelineData {
49:   return {
50:     ...input,
51:     sources: input.sources.filter((v) => membership.sources.has(v.id)),
52:     records: input.records.filter((v) => membership.records.has(v.id)),
53:     findings: input.findings.filter((v) => membership.findings.has(v.id)),
54:     themes: input.themes.filter((v) => membership.themes.has(v.id)),
55:     requirements: input.requirements.filter((v) => membership.requirements.has(v.id)),
56:   };
57: }

59: /**
60:  * Dependency closure. Supporting context may occur on several branches; primary items never do.
61:  * For requirements, themes connected to cited findings are contextual clusters, including siblings.
62:  * Missing referenced entities remain missing and are reported, never fabricated or removed from IDs.
63:  */
64: export function evidenceIndex(input: PipelineData, log: (message: string) => void) {
65:   const primary = primaryLayer(input);
66:   const maps = {
67:     sources: new Map(input.sources.map((v) => [v.id, v])),
68:     records: new Map(input.records.map((v) => [v.id, v])),
69:     findings: new Map(input.findings.map((v) => [v.id, v])),
70:     themes: new Map(input.themes.map((v) => [v.id, v])),
71:     requirements: new Map(input.requirements.map((v) => [v.id, v])),
72:   };
73:   const positions = new Map(
74:     DATA_KEYS.flatMap((key) => input[key].map((item, index) => [item.id, index] as const)),
75:   );
76:   function selected<T extends { id: string }>(map: Map<string, T>, ids: Set<string>): T[] {
77:     return [...ids]
78:       .map((id) => map.get(id)!)
79:       .sort((a, b) => positions.get(a.id)! - positions.get(b.id)!);
80:   }
81:   const themesByFinding = new Map<string, Set<string>>();
82:   const findingsByTheme = new Map<string, Set<string>>();
83:   for (const theme of input.themes) {
84:     for (const findingId of theme.findingIds) {
85:       const ids = themesByFinding.get(findingId) ?? new Set<string>();
86:       ids.add(theme.id);
87:       themesByFinding.set(findingId, ids);
88:     }
89:   }
90:   for (const finding of input.findings) {
91:     if (!finding.themeId) continue;
92:     const ids = findingsByTheme.get(finding.themeId) ?? new Set<string>();
93:     ids.add(finding.id);
94:     findingsByTheme.set(finding.themeId, ids);
95:   }
96:   const warned = new Set<string>();
97:   function missing(key: DataKey, id: string) {
98:     const ref = `${key}:${id}`;
99:     if (!warned.has(ref))
100:       log(`Unavailable referenced ${key} ${id}; retaining original link, no evidence invented.`);
101:     warned.add(ref);
102:   }
103:   return {
104:     /** Build small prompt contexts from indexes, not one full input scan per primary item. */
105:     context(membership: Membership): PipelineData {
106:       return {
107:         ...input,
108:         sources: selected(maps.sources, membership.sources),
109:         records: selected(maps.records, membership.records),
110:         findings: selected(maps.findings, membership.findings),
111:         themes: selected(maps.themes, membership.themes),
112:         requirements: selected(maps.requirements, membership.requirements),
113:       };
114:     },
115:     closure(layer: DataKey, id: string): Membership {
116:       const membership = emptyMembership();
117:       function add(key: DataKey, ref: string): void {
118:         if (membership[key].has(ref)) return;
119:         if (!maps[key].has(ref)) {
120:           missing(key, ref);
121:           return;
122:         }
123:         membership[key].add(ref);
124:         switch (key) {
125:           case "requirements": {
126:             const requirement = maps.requirements.get(ref)!;
127:             const findingIds = [...requirement.findingIds, ...requirement.conflictingFindingIds];
128:             for (const findingId of findingIds) {
129:               add("findings", findingId);
130:               for (const themeId of themesByFinding.get(findingId) ?? []) add("themes", themeId);
131:               const themeId = maps.findings.get(findingId)?.themeId;
132:               if (themeId) add("themes", themeId);
133:             }
134:             for (const sourceId of requirement.sourceIds) add("sources", sourceId);
135:             break;
136:           }
137:           case "themes": {
138:             for (const findingId of maps.themes.get(ref)!.findingIds) add("findings", findingId);
139:             for (const findingId of findingsByTheme.get(ref) ?? []) add("findings", findingId);
140:             break;
141:           }
142:           case "findings": {
143:             const finding = maps.findings.get(ref)!;
144:             // Supporting themes may be shared; classified primary themes must not be duplicated.
145:             if (finding.themeId && primary !== "themes") add("themes", finding.themeId);
146:             for (const evidence of finding.evidence) {
147:               add("sources", evidence.sourceId);
148:               if (evidence.recordId) add("records", evidence.recordId);
149:             }
150:             break;
151:           }
152:           case "records":
153:             add("sources", maps.records.get(ref)!.sourceId);
154:             break;
155:           case "sources":
156:             break;
157:         }
158:       }
159:       add(layer, id);
160:       return membership;
161:     },
162:   };
163: }

166: export function retainOrphans(
167:   input: PipelineData,
168:   memberships: Membership[],
169:   index: ReturnType<typeof evidenceIndex>,
170:   log: (message: string) => void,
171: ): void {
172:   const first = memberships.find((membership) => DATA_KEYS.some((key) => membership[key].size));
173:   if (!first) return;
174:   const counts: string[] = [];
175:   for (const key of DATA_KEYS) {
176:     const referenced = new Set(memberships.flatMap((membership) => [...membership[key]]));
177:     const orphans = input[key].filter((item) => !referenced.has(item.id));
178:     for (const item of orphans) {
179:       const closure = index.closure(key, item.id);
180:       for (const dependencyKey of DATA_KEYS) {
181:         for (const id of closure[dependencyKey]) first[dependencyKey].add(id);
182:       }
183:     }
184:     if (orphans.length) counts.push(`${orphans.length} ${key}`);
185:   }
186:   if (counts.length)
187:     log(
188:       `Retained orphan upstream context (${counts.join(", ")}) once on out-${memberships.indexOf(first)} with dependency closure; evidence may be shared, not independently classified.`,
189:     );
190: }
